common.technicalOverviewIntro: A quick look at the tools and structure behind this portfolio.
common.technicalOverviewCoreDescription: React 19 and TypeScript, built with Vite and routed with React Router.
common.technicalOverviewUiDescription: Styled-components, shared theme tokens, and React Icons.
common.technicalOverviewAnimationDescription: Motion for React transitions and GSAP for the FoldText interaction.
common.technicalOverviewFormsDescription: React Hook Form handles contact form state and validation; Web3Forms processes submissions.
common.technicalOverviewServicesDescription: Static hosting on Netlify, Cloudflare Web Analytics, Supabase Storage for the CV, and Web3Forms for contact delivery. Supabase Storage is used only to host the public CV/document file; it is not used as a database or application backend.
common.technicalOverviewServicesMobileDescripti: Netlify hosting, Cloudflare analytics, Supabase Storage for the public CV only (not a database or backend), and Web3Forms for contact delivery.
common.technicalOverviewArchitectureDescription: Page-based routes, shared components, separated portfolio data, and centralized theme styles.
common.technicalOverviewStructure:
src/
├─ assets/       images and fonts
├─ components/   shared UI, header, footer
├─ data/         portfolio content
├─ pages/        route views
└─ styles/       global styles and theme

public/
└─ static files and redirects

about.heading: What I do
about.lead: I've been working in frontend for more than seven years, mostly with React, JavaScript and TypeScript.
about.intro1: I've worked on products in finance, energy, lottery and legal services, both on new projects and on existing applications that needed new features, migrations, fixes or cleanup.
about.intro2: Most of my work revolves around building and maintaining interfaces, integrating APIs, managing state, improving performance and keeping the codebase understandable over time.
about.approachLead: I like understanding the problem before touching the code.
about.approach1: I usually look at the requirements, the existing code and the possible approaches first. I prefer simple, maintainable solutions over clever ones that make things harder later.
about.approach2: If something isn't clear, I ask. If I take ownership of something, I like to follow it through to the end.
about.seniority1: Being senior doesn't mean having an answer for everything.
about.seniority2: For me, it means knowing how to investigate a problem, understand the trade-offs, make a decision and explain it.
about.seniority3: It also means helping the team. I enjoy code reviews, technical discussions and helping less experienced developers when I can.
about.seniority4: I use AI tools too, mainly to explore ideas, compare approaches and speed up repetitive work. I still want to understand what I'm putting into the codebase.
about.outside1: Cinema has always been one of my biggest interests. I like films, but also everything behind them: photography, editing, sound and filmmaking.
about.outside2: Over the years, I've also experimented with amateur filmmaking and nature timelapses.
about.outside3: Archery is another thing I enjoy. It takes patience, concentration and a lot of small adjustments. Pretty close to debugging, actually.
about.outside4: Above all, I'm a dad. That probably teaches me more about patience and priorities than anything else.
about.signature: I like things that make sense, work well, and don't need to shout about it.
